newsitem.title: UK: Bond markets consolidate in week, OATs hit - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Bond markets consolidate in week, OATs hit - Salomon.

text.p: Most bond markets were steady in the latest week, according to data from Salomon Brothers on Friday.
Politics-ridden France suffered the biggest losses in the week ended April 23, the bank's world government bond index showed. The overall index was up 0.06 percent on the week.

French OATs posted a loss of 0.31 percent in local currency terms in the week. French President Jacques Chirac on Monday announced an early election for late May/early June, sparking uncertainty for French debt investors.
The top markets were Switzerland, Finland and Canada.
Swiss bonds returned 0.39 percent in the week in Swiss franc terms. Finnish debt gave investors 0.36 percent and Canadian bonds made a gain of 0.30 percent in local currency terms.

For dollar based investors, Danish debt was the best play, giving 1.15 percent in dollar terms. Core European bonds also did well, with Austrian bonds returning 1.12 percent, Bunds 1.11 percent and Dutch debt 1.05 percent in the week.

The biggest loser for dollar based investors was Japan, one of only three markets to lose ground in this respect. Japanese government bonds shed 0.32 percent in dollar terms, while Italian BTPs lost 0.24 percent and British gilts a slim 0.01 percent.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
